data.title: Aham Vaishvanaro Bhuthva
data.description: Aham Vaishvanaro Bhutva means "I, having become the universal fire," and in Bhagavad Gita 15.14 Krishna says he lives in every body and digests its food. United with the prana and apana breaths, this inner fire cooks the four kinds of food: chewed, swallowed, licked and sucked. Families often say it before a meal to treat eating as an offering.

verses.title: Aham Vaishvanaro Bhuthva – Verse 1
verses.sanskrit:
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः
प्राणापान समायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम्
verses.transliteration:
ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ
prāṇāpāna samāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidham
